articles.title: New car sales in Esterhavn rose 12.4% last year
articles.description: Esterhavn sold 412,000 new vehicles last year, up 12.4% year on year, with imports making up most of the growth.
articles.content:
New vehicle sales in Esterhavn rose 12.4% last year to about 412,000 units, the national dealers' association said.
Passenger cars accounted for roughly two thirds of the total, while light commercial vehicles made up most of the rest.
Imported models supplied nearly 60% of the light vehicle market, up from about half a year earlier.
Compact crossovers were the best-selling segment for the second year running.
Sales of fully electric cars more than doubled, though they still made up less than 5% of the market.
The association said lower lending rates and a wider choice of budget models helped lift demand.
Local assembly plants produced fewer cars than the year before as two factories retooled for new models.
The government has promised new incentives for local manufacturing under its long-term vehicle plan.

articles.title: Marovia orders coal plants to run at full output
articles.description: Marovia orders coal plants to run at full output
articles.content:
Marovia's energy ministry has told all coal-fired power stations to run at full output for the next two months.
The order follows a heat wave that pushed electricity demand to a record on several days this month.
Hydropower output has fallen because of low rainfall in the northern catchments.
Officials said plants that had planned maintenance would have to postpone it unless they faced safety risks.
Grid operator figures show evening peak demand exceeding supply by a small margin on at least four days.
The ministry invoked an emergency provision that allows it to direct generators to operate power stations in line with its instructions.

articles.title: Harborline Bank drops points transfers to Skyward Rewards
articles.description: Harborline Bank credit cards no longer let members move points to Skyward Rewards, leaving two airline programmes as the main options.
articles.content:
Harborline Bank has quietly removed Skyward Rewards from the list of airline programmes its cardholders can transfer points to.
The change took effect this week, according to an updated rewards catalogue on the bank's website.
Members can still convert points to Coastline Miles and Aurora Club, the two programmes most readers use.
What this means
Skyward was never the best-value option on Harborline cards, because the conversion rate was poorer than for the other partners.
Still, it was useful for travellers who wanted to top up an existing Skyward balance for a specific award seat.
Anyone holding points they intended to move to Skyward should look at the remaining partners or at other card issuers.
Several other banks still offer transfers to Skyward, though usually at a lower ratio.
